title: week 8
introduction: This week, we explored the relationship between art, design and technology, starting with the Bauhaus and moving on to speculative design and planetary art. I was particularly interested in how speculative design can help us explore complex problems by questioning existing systems and imagining alternative futures, rather than simply providing solutions.
related_work: Two projects from the lecture caught my attention.The Extinction Gong (2017) by Julian Oliver and Crystelle Vu, and Rare Earthenware (2018) by Unknown Fields. The Extinction Gong uses sound to make species extinction more perceptible, while Rare Earthenware uses toxic waste from rare-earth processing to reveal the hidden environmental costs of electronic products. Both projects made me think about how art can communicate complex environmental issues through different sensory experiences.
method: For this week's assignment, I chose to focus on speculative design. I used Rare Earthenware as a starting point and connected it with my previous research on the environmental impact of headphones in my Creative Coding project. I also considered systems thinking to explore how different stages of a product's lifecycle are connected, including production, use, repair and disposal.
results_discussion: One concept I found particularly useful this week was systems thinking. I initially found it difficult to distinguish between systems thinking, cybernetics and speculative design. Through further reflection, I began to understand that systems thinking focuses on the relationships between different elements, while cybernetics examines how feedback influences the behaviour of a system. Speculative design can draw on these ideas to explore possible futures and question existing assumptions.The lecture also made me think more about how artists choose to communicate complex information. The Extinction Gong transforms statistical information into sound, while Rare Earthenware uses physical materials to reveal environmental impacts. Both approaches make issues that are normally difficult to perceive more tangible. However, I also wonder whether making a problem visible or perceptible is enough to influence people's behaviour. An audience might understand the message of an artwork without necessarily changing their actions.This made me realise that the way an audience experiences information is just as important as the information itself. I am interested in how interaction might encourage people to think more actively, rather than simply receive a message.
conclusion_future_work: This week helped me understand that design does not always need to provide immediate solutions. It can also encourage people to question existing assumptions and consider the wider consequences of their decisions. In my future work, I would like to explore how interactive experiences can help audiences understand complex systems and reflect on their own actions.
